'''Kemba Hudley Walker''' (born May 8, 1990)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kemba Walker Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/walkeke02.html|access-date=November 8, 2020|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is a player enhancement coach for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was picked ninth overall by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]] and also played for the [[Boston Celtics]], [[New York Knicks]], and the [[Dallas Mavericks]], before finishing his career with [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut Huskies]]. In their [[2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|2010–11 season]], Walker was the nation's second-leading scorer and was named consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]; he also led the Huskies to a [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2011 NCAA championship]] victory and claimed the tournament's [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] award.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harris |first=Jarrel |date=2014-03-21 |title=We Reminisce: Kemba Walker’s 2011 NCAA Tournament Run |url=https://uproxx.com/dimemag/reminisce-kemba-walkers-2011-ncaa-tournament-run/ |access-date=2025-07-13 |website=UPROXX |language=en-US}}</ref> Walker is a four-time [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]], a one-time [[All-NBA Team]] member, two-time winner of the [[NBA Sportsmanship Award]], as well as a [[LNB Élite]] champion.

==High school career==
Walker attended [[Rice High School (New York)|Rice High School]] in [[Harlem]], New York City. During his junior year, Walker played once at [[Madison Square Garden]] against [[Simeon Career Academy]] and senior guard [[Derrick Rose]] in a 53–51 victory.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=USA Today | url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2007-01-11-rose-new-york_x.htm?POE=SPOISVA|title=Chicago standout Rose takes stage in New York|author=Lawlor, Christopher |date=January 11, 2007 |access-date=January 30, 2011}}</ref> Over his senior year, he posted 18.2 points and 5.3 assists per game,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/EqSVKSBT_EGXkzbOjv4oFA/basketball-winter-07-08/stats-kemba-walker.htm|title=Kemba Walker Rice Basketball Stats 07-08|publisher=MaxPreps|access-date=June 21, 2009|archive-date=July 21, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721231404/http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/EqSVKSBT_EGXkzbOjv4oFA/basketball-winter-07-08/stats-kemba-walker.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> earning him a spot on the prestigious [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American Team]]. He was able to play in the elite New York City Gauchos, the premier [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball program for youth, and was joined by fellow [[Big East Conference]] talents-to-be [[Jordan Theodore]], [[Darryl Bryant]], Liam Herman, and Liam Arazi. Walker's team finished No. 1 in the nation.

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Walker was listed as the No. 5 point guard and the No. 14 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Kemba-Walker-60134;_ylt=AtaUVxIThdBQ0CpL8e3fuhFGPZB4|title=Rivals.com|publisher=Yahoo! Sport}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman year===
During his freshman year at the [[University of Connecticut]], Walker played in every contest and was named to the Big East All-Rookie Team. He helped the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|Huskies]] achieve a number one seed in the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2009 NCAA tournament]]. Despite starting in only two games, he averaged 25.5 minutes per contest, far more than any regular non-starter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/teams/stats?teamId=41|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080123221430/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/teams/stats?teamId=41|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 23, 2008|title=Connecticut Huskies 2016–17 Statistics – Team and Player Stats – Men's College Basketball|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> He also helped the Huskies advance to the 2009 [[Final Four]] with a 23-point effort in the [[Elite Eight]] versus [[University of Missouri|Missouri]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2009-03-28/sports/17917608_1_freshman-kemba-walker-uconn-missouri|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130130125702/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2009-03-28/sports/17917608_1_freshman-kemba-walker-uconn-missouri|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 30, 2013|title=Freshman Kemba Walker's 23 points helps UConn outlast Missouri|author =Roger Rubin|newspaper= [[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]] |date=March 28, 2009}}</ref>

===Sophomore year===
During the Huskies' 2009–2010 season, Walker started in all 34 of their games and contributed an average of 14.6 points. He also led the team in scoring for the eighth time in the last nine games of the season, with 18 points at [[Virginia Tech]]. Walker was named by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|U.S. Basketball Writers Association (USBWA)]] to the First Team All-District. Connecticut clinched a 4-seed in the NCAA's [[2010 National Invitation Tournament]] only to fall short to [[Virginia Tech]] and finish the relatively disappointing season going 18–16 (7–11) in conference play.<ref name="uconnprofile">{{cite web|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kemba_walker_714048.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140711080231/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kemba_walker_714048.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 11, 2014 |title=Kemba Walker Bio |work=UConnHuskies.com |access-date=July 9, 2014 }}</ref>

===Junior year===
[[File:Kemba Walker 2011.jpg|thumb|Walker with [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]] in 2011]]
Walker rose to national prominence in his third year at Connecticut. This was because, twelve games into his junior campaign, he distinguished himself as the leading scorer in the nation, posting 26.7 points per contest; in addition, Walker averaged 5 rebounds and 3.8 assists. It was then that he appeared on one of the six regional covers of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' magazine.

In the [[2011 Big East men's basketball tournament|2011 Big East tournament]], Walker hit the game-clinching shot at the buzzer to beat Brad Wannamaker and the [[2010–11 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh Panthers]], ranked No. 3 overall, thereby advancing the Huskies to the semifinals. Walker led UConn to victory in the ensuing Big East Championship against the [[2010–11 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville Cardinals]] and earned tournament MVP honors in the process. Over five games in as many days, Walker tallied an unprecedented 130 points, a record of points scored for not only the Big East but for any conference tournament in the past 15 seasons. UConn thus became the first school to win five games in five days and earn a conference championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310710097 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160806222911/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310710097 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 6, 2016 |title=Connecticut Huskies vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap |publisher=ESPN |date=March 12, 2011 |access-date=March 22, 2011}}</ref>

On March 14, 2011, the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|U.S. Basketball Writers Association]] named Walker First Team All-American<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.theday.com/article/20110314/INTERACT010103/110319839 |title=Walker named All-American |publisher=The Day |date=March 14, 2011 |access-date=March 22, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323050508/http://www.theday.com/article/20110314/INTERACT010103/110319839 |archive-date=March 23, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> with only [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] picking him to the Second Team.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010–11 All-America teams |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |date=March 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }}</ref> His heroic performance in the 2010–11 season also made him a finalist for the Association's college player of the year honors, the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]]. Despite finishing second to national sensation Jimmer Fredette for this award, at least several journalists held that it was rather Walker who deserved the distinction of best player that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/Jeff-Goodman-Brilliant-Kemba-Walker-paces-Connecticuts-run-to-Big-East-title-031211|title=Hard to argue Walker's POY candidacy – FOX Sports|date=March 12, 2011}}
* {{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2011/03/12/2011-03-12_bronx_product_kemba_walker_has_dazzled_fans_with_clutch_play_at_uconn.html|title=Bronx product dazzles fans with clutch play|website=[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]]|location=New York}}</ref> Among other accolades bestowed on him, Walker claimed the [[Bob Cousy Award]] for college basketball's top point guard in the nation.<ref>[http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2011-03-30/report-kemba-walker-wins-bob-cousy-award Report: Kemba Walker wins Bob Cousy Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110401205427/http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2011-03-30/report-kemba-walker-wins-bob-cousy-award |date=April 1, 2011 }}. Retrieved March 31, 2011</ref> On April 4, 2011, Walker, with 16 points himself, rallied and led the University of Connecticut to win the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Division I Championship]], while he won the honor of [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/The-Unlikelys-Butler-and-UConn-play-for-it-all-01220612|title=UConn defeats Butler 53–41 for 3rd national title, Fox Sports, Associated Press|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017231309/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/The-Unlikelys-Butler-and-UConn-play-for-it-all-01220612|archive-date=October 17, 2012}}</ref> Upon the team's return from Houston, at a pep rally to celebrate the National Title, Walker was added to the [[Huskies of Honor]]. He became the first men's basketball player to receive the distinction since the inaugural class was announced in December 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mysanantonio.com/default/article/UConn-Men-Celebrate-With-Thousands-of-Fans-Kemba-1324249.php|title=UConn Men Celebrate With Thousands of Fans; Kemba Walker's Jersey Retired. ''Journal Register News Service'', April 5, 2011}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Charlotte Bobcats/Hornets (2011–2019)===
====2011–12 season: Rookie season====
[[File:Kemba Walker vs Rockets1.JPG|thumb|Walker shoots during a game against the [[Houston Rockets]], October 2013]]
Walker graduated from UConn in three years. Accordingly, he entered the [[2011 NBA draft]] and was selected ninth overall by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sources: Kemba Walker going pro |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=6331070 |publisher=ESPN |date=April 12, 2011 |access-date=April 12, 2011}}</ref> Walker signed a multi-year shoe deal with [[Under Armour]], the first rookie from the 2011 draft class to do so.<ref name="Under Armour">{{cite web|title=Kemba Walker signs multi-year deal with Under Armour|url=http://www.digitalsportscene.com/forum/nba-ncaa-basketball/17730-kemba-walker-signs-multi-year-deal-under-armour.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170714083325/http://www.digitalsportscene.com/forum/nba-ncaa-basketball/17730-kemba-walker-signs-multi-year-deal-under-armour.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 14, 2017|publisher=Digital Sports Scene|access-date=July 5, 2011}}</ref>

On December 11, 2011, he signed the rookie scale contract with the Bobcats,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_kemba_walker_111211.html |title=Charlotte Bobcats Sign Guard Kemba Walker |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |date=December 11, 2011 |access-date=December 12, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126101943/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_kemba_walker_111211.html |archive-date=January 26, 2012 }}</ref> and with the injury of point guard [[D. J. Augustin]], he became their starting point guard for the lockout-shortened season. Walker participated in the 2012 [[Rising Stars Challenge]] during [[NBA All-Star Weekend|All-Star Weekend]]. However, the Charlotte Bobcats only managed to go 7–59 in the lockout season.

====2012–13 season: Sophomore season====
On November 14, 2012, Walker hit the first game-winner of his NBA career against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aw_lWY_doLc | archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211030/aw_lWY_doLc| archive-date=October 30, 2021| title=Kemba's game-winner in Minnesota! | via=YouTube | date=November 14, 2012 | access-date=January 9, 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He finished the game with 22 points on 9-of-19 shooting, as well as 5 rebounds, 4 assists and 4 steals.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121114/CHAMIN/gameinfo.html | title=Notebook: Bobcats 89, Timberwolves 87 | publisher=National Basketball Association | date=November 14, 2012 | access-date=January 9, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330123011/http://www.nba.com/games/20121114/CHAMIN/gameinfo.html | archive-date=March 30, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 21, 2013, he scored a then career-high 35 points against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kemba_walker/career_stats.html|title=Kemba Walker Career Stats|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116174751/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kemba_walker/career_stats.html|archive-date=January 16, 2014}}</ref> During the 2012–13 season, Walker was selected with teammate [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]] to the [[2013 NBA All-Star Game|2013 Rising Stars Challenge]] in which they both scored 8 points.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/allstar/NBA_2013_rookie.html|title = 2013 NBA Rising Stars Box Score}}</ref>

Kemba finished the 2012–13 season with averages of 17.7 points, 5.8 assists, 3.5 rebounds, and 2 steals per contest. He took significant strides over his rookie year.

====2013–14 season: First playoff appearance====
[[File:Bobcats vs Nets 8.jpg|thumb|Walker defended by [[Gerald Wallace]] in 2013]]
On December 18, 2013, Walker hit a buzzer-beating jump shot over [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] in overtime to beat the Toronto Raptors. He finished the night with 26 points and 5 rebounds on 10/18 shooting from the field.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/12/19/bobcats-kemba-walker-drains-overtime-game-winner-to-beat-raptors-video/|title=Bobcats' Kemba Walker drains overtime game winner to beat Raptors (VIDEO)|date=December 19, 2013}}</ref> On February 19, 2014, Walker recorded 23 points, 5 rebounds and a career-high 16 assists in a 116–98 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489674 | title=Jefferson leads Bobcats over Pistons again 116–98 | publisher=ESPN | date=February 19, 2014 | access-date=January 9, 2015}}</ref> Five days later, he was awarded the Eastern Conference Player of the Week, having averaged 22.5 points, 8.8 assists, and 5.5 rebounds in the span of seven days. In a home victory over the Orlando Magic on April 4, 2014, Walker recorded his second career triple-double with 13 points, 10 assists, and 10 rebounds.

Playing against the [[Miami Heat]] in the first round of the Eastern Conference Playoffs and with teammate [[Al Jefferson]] unable to play due to a [[Plantar fasciitis]] injury, Walker had an exceptional game four: he finished the game with a playoff franchise-high 29 points, along with 5 assists, 5 rebounds, 3 blocks, and 2 steals. The effort came in a loss as the Heat completed a four-game sweep of the Bobcats.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140428/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|title=Heat at Bobcats|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=May 10, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208230153/http://www.nba.com/games/20140428/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 8, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2014–15 season: Knee surgery====
[[File:Wizards-Hornets (October 17, 2014).jpg|thumb|Walker with the Hornets in October 2014]]
In the newly renamed Charlotte Hornets' opening game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on October 29, Walker led an impressive comeback in an overtime 108–106 victory. The Hornets had been 24 points down by the fourth quarter when they staged a comeback; Walker scored a three-pointer with 1.6 seconds left to force overtime and later hit the shot that clinched the game as well. He finished with 26 points, 5 assists, and 6 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/MILCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Bucks at Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=October 30, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221200618/http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/MILCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 21, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following day, he signed a four-year, $48 million contract extension with the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-walker-multi-year-extension|title=Hornets Sign Walker to Multi-Year Extension – Charlotte Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}
* {{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11781139/kemba-walker-charlotte-hornets-agree-contract-extension|title=Source: Hornets' Walker extended 4 years|date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> On December 5, 2014, Walker hit his second game-winner of the season in a 103–102 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141205/NYKCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Knicks at Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref> On December 27, in a 94–102 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]], he scored a then career-high 42 points and set a Charlotte Hornets franchise record for most points scored in a half with his 35 points that he posted in the second.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141227/ORLCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Magic at Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=December 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230021055/http://www.nba.com/games/20141227/ORLCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 30, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 3, against the Orlando Magic, Walker scored 30 points to pass [[Kendall Gill]] for 10th place on the Charlotte Hornets all-time scoring list with 4,160 points.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400578787 | title=Kemba Walker scores 30 points as Hornets halt 5-game skid | publisher=ESPN | date=January 3, 2015 | access-date=January 9, 2015}}</ref> In three back-to-back games played between the January 3 and 7, Walker scored 30, 33, and 31 points in victories over the [[Orlando Magic]], the [[Boston Celtics]], and the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] respectively; he thereby joined [[Larry Johnson (basketball, born 1969)|Larry Johnson]], [[Glen Rice]], and [[Kelly Tripucka]] as one of four players in Charlotte Hornets' franchise history to have three or more consecutive games of scoring 30-plus points.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://twitter.com/rvarner/status/553217223301799937/ | title=Russell Varner – For anyone curious where... | via=Twitter | date=January 8, 2015 | access-date=January 9, 2015}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=July 2023}} Walker also hit his fifth game-winner of his career and his third of the season on January 7 in the 98–94 victory over the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/media/slam-tv/kemba-walker-banks-game-winner-vs-pelicans-video/|title=Kemba Walker Banks in Game-Winner vs the Pelicans (VIDEO)|date=January 8, 2015}}</ref> On January 12, he was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, January 5, through Sunday, January 11. Over the week, he led the Hornets to a 4–0 record and averaged 30.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 4.5 assists in 36.2 minutes, while shooting .500 from the field (44–88), .364 from beyond the three-point line (8–22) and .893 from the free-throw line (25–28).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-guard-kemba-walker-named-eastern-conference-player-week|title=Hornets Guard Kemba Walker Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week – Charlotte Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref>

On January 28, 2015, Walker was ruled out for six weeks after he underwent successful surgery to repair a torn lateral meniscus in his left knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/walker-has-successful-surgery|title=Walker Has Successful Surgery – Charlotte Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref> He returned to action on March 11, after missing 18 games, to score six points in 16 minutes off the bench as the Hornets lost to the Sacramento Kings 106–113.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150311/SACCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Kings at Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref>

====2015–16 season: Breakthrough====
On November 23, 2015, Walker scored a then season-high 39 points in a 127–122 overtime win over the Sacramento Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151123/SACCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Kings vs Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=November 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126210235/http://www.nba.com/games/20151123/SACCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 26, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 18, 2016, Walker set a career-high and a franchise-record with 52 points in a 124–119 double overtime win over the Utah Jazz. He made 16-of-34 from the field, including 6-of-11 three-pointers, and was 14-of-15 from the free throw line, breaking the team mark of 48 points set by [[Glen Rice]] in March 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160118/UTACHA/gameinfo.html|title=Jazz vs Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=January 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122191019/http://www.nba.com/games/20160118/UTACHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 22, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 9, in a win over the New Orleans Pelicans, Walker became just the third Hornets player to make 500 career three-pointers, joining [[Dell Curry]] (929) and [[Glen Rice]] (508).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160309/NOPCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Pelicans vs Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=March 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626222927/https://www.nba.com/games/20160309/NOPCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=June 26, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> Five days later, he earned his fourth career Player of the Week award, and second of the 2015–16 season (first coming on January 25),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-guard-kemba-walker-named-eastern-conference-player-week-0|title=Hornets Guard Kemba Walker Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week – Charlotte Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref> becoming just the sixth Charlotte player to win the award multiple times in the same season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/kemba-walker-named-eastern-conference-player-week|title=Kemba Walker Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week – Charlotte Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref> The Hornets finished the regular season as the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference with a 48–34 record. In the first round of the playoffs, the Hornets faced the third-seeded Miami Heat, and in a Game 4 win on April 25, Walker scored a playoff career-high 34 points, helping the Hornets tie the series at 2–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160425/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|title=Heat vs Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=April 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160426052843/http://www.nba.com/games/20160425/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 26, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He topped that mark in Game 6 of the series, scoring 37 points in a 97–90 loss, as the Heat tied the series at 3–3.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160429/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|title=Heat vs Hornets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501180909/http://www.nba.com/games/20160429/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 1, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Hornets went on to lose Game 7, bowing out of the playoffs with a 4–3 defeat.

In May 2016, Walker again underwent surgery on a torn meniscus in his left knee.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2016/05/09/charlotte-hornets-kemba-walker-torn-meniscus-surgery|title=Walker undergoes surgery on torn meniscus|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=May 9, 2016}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2019–2021)===
Coming off a frustrating [[2018–19 Boston Celtics season|2018–19 season]], the [[Boston Celtics]] would go on to lose franchise centerpieces [[Kyrie Irving]] and [[Al Horford]] to free agency, opening the door to start a new chapter with a new max-salary player. After Walker and the Celtics showed mutual interest at the start of free agency, he officially joined the franchise on July 6, 2019, through a [[sign and trade]] deal with [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte]] worth $141 million over four years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-three-time-all-star-kemba-walker|title=Celtics Acquire Three-Time All-Star Kemba Walker|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> Walker chose to wear [[Kobe Bryant]]’s number 8 with the Celtics as his usual number 15 had been retired by the Celtics in honor of [[Tom Heinsohn]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nesn.com/2019/07/why-8-kemba-walker-explains-reason-behind-celtics-jersey-number/|title = Why 8? Kemba Walker Explains Reason Behind Celtics Jersey Number|date = July 17, 2019}}</ref>

Walker made his Celtics debut on October 23, 2019, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]; he put up 12 points on 18 [[Field goal (basketball)|shot attempts from the field]] in 34 minutes of play during the 107–93 loss.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401160630|title=Celtics vs. 76ers – Box Score – October 23, 2019|publisher=ESPN|access-date=October 24, 2019}}</ref> On November 22, during a game against the Nuggets, Walker went down with a neck injury after colliding with teammate Semi Ojeleye. He was taken off the court on a stretcher. He was first diagnosed with concussion-like symptoms, and then later diagnosed with a sprained neck. On November 27, Walker scored a then season-high 39 points in a 121–110 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game?gameId=401160895|title = Nets vs. Celtics – Game Summary – November 27, 2019 – ESPN}}</ref> That season-high would be eclipsed on December 11, when Walker scored 44 points in 122–117 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game?gameId=401160999|title = Celtics vs. Pacers – Game Summary – December 11, 2019 – ESPN}}</ref> On January 16, 2020, Walker would post a 40-point, 11 assist [[double-double (basketball)|double-double]] in a 128–123 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game?gameId=401161257|title = Celtics vs. Bucks – Game Summary – January 16, 2020 – ESPN}}</ref>

On January 20, Walker recorded his first head-to-head win against [[LeBron James]], after having begun his career 0–28 against him. Posting 20 points, seven assists, four rebounds, and a steal, he helped the Celtics come away with a 139–107 blowout victory over longtime [[Celtics–Lakers rivalry|rivals]] the [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2872354-kemba-walker-on-1st-head-to-head-win-vs-lebron-james-its-only-1-1-28|title=Kemba Walker on 1st Head-to-Head Win vs. LeBron James: 'It's Only 1. ... 1–28.'|website=Bleacher Report|date=January 20, 2020|access-date=January 23, 2020}}</ref> Three days later, Walker was named to his fourth consecutive [[2020 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]], being selected as an Eastern Conference starter.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/amp/league/article/2020/01/23/2020-all-star-starters-and-captains-announced |title=Captains LeBron James, Giannis Antetokounmpo headline starters for NBA All-Star 2020 |publisher=National Basketball Association |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200125004946/https://www.nba.com/amp/league/article/2020/01/23/2020-all-star-starters-and-captains-announced |archive-date=January 25, 2020}}</ref>

The [[2019–20 Boston Celtics season|2019–2020 season]] was suspended due to the COVID-19 pandemic. After the season resumed, Walker helped the Celtics reach the Eastern Conference Finals, where the team was defeated by the [[Miami Heat]]. Walker missed several games during the season due to knee soreness.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/misc-070920-2019-20-season-refresh-kemba-walker|title=2019–20 Season Refresh: Kemba Walker|website=Boston Celtics}}</ref>

|archive-date=December 28, 2021 |access-date=December 28, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=}}</ref>

Walker missed games in January 2022 due to knee problems.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bondy |first=Stefan |date=January 6, 2022 |title=Kemba Walker out again; Derrick Rose, not Julius Randle, on first returns of fan All-Star ballot |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-kemba-walker-julius-randle-20220107-xmizutzee5ezvfswb32ogcqq3e-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220107154004/https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-kemba-walker-julius-randle-20220107-xmizutzee5ezvfswb32ogcqq3e-story.html |archive-date=January 7, 2022 |access-date=July 2, 2024 |website=[[New York Daily News]] |location=}}</ref> In February 2022, the Knicks and Walker reached an agreement that he would be sidelined for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 23, 2022 |title=New York Knicks, Kemba Walker agree he'll be sidelined rest of season, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33355902/new-york-knicks-kemba-walker-agree-sidelined-rest-season-sources-say |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224205911/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33355902/new-york-knicks-kemba-walker-agree-sidelined-rest-season-sources-say |archive-date=February 24, 2022 |access-date=February 23, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2022–2023)===
On July 6, 2022, Walker and the draft rights to [[Jalen Duren]] were traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for a future first-round selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-acquire-future-first-round-draft-pick|title=Knicks Acquire Future First Round Draft Pick|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 6, 2022}}</ref> On October 17, Walker reached a contract buyout agreement with the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sankofa II |first1=Omari |title=Detroit Pistons waive veteran guard Kemba Walker, costing them $9.2 million |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/10/17/detroit-pistons-nba-waive-kemba-walker-contract/69565340007/ |website=Detroit Free Press |access-date=October 23, 2022 |date=October 17, 2022}}</ref>

On November 28, 2022, Walker signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], on a one-year, non-guaranteed deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mavericks add Kemba Walker to bolster ballhandling|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-kemba|date=November 29, 2022|website=mavs.com|access-date=November 29, 2022}}</ref> On December 17, Walker put up a season-high 32 points, five rebounds, and seven assists in a 100–99 overtime loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavs-news-kemba-walker-explosion-sparks-jalen-brunson-2-0-dreams-for-dallas-fans|title=Kemba Walker explosion sparks Jalen Brunson 2.0 dreams for Mavs fans|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=December 17, 2022|access-date=December 17, 2022}}</ref> On January 6, 2023, Walker was waived by the Mavericks.<ref>{{Cite news|title=The Mavericks waive Kemba Walker after brief nine-game stint to create minutes for younger guards|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/mavericks-waive-kemba-walker-after-brief-nine-game-stint-to-create-minutes-for-younger-guards/|access-date=April 20, 2023|work=CBS Sports|first=Sam|last=Quinn|date=January 6, 2023}}</ref>

===AS Monaco (2023–2024)===
On July 21, 2023, Walker signed with [[LNB Pro A]] and [[EuroLeague]] club [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]], moving outside of the United States for the first time in his career.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=AS Monaco Basket|title=ᴋᴇᴍʙᴀ ᴡᴀʟᴋᴇʀ ᴇsᴛ ᴍᴏɴéɢᴀsǫᴜᴇ 🔴⚪️ ✍️ L'AS Monaco est heureuse d'annoncer la signature pour la saison à venir du meneur américain 🇺🇸 4️⃣ fois All-Star 🌟 le meilleur marqueur de l'histoire des Charlotte Hornets (12 009 points) a disputé 750 matchs en NBA 🔛 🚀 Scoreur d'exception, il apportera son expérience et sa maestria à la mène en Principauté 🇲🇨|number=1682371254076973057|user=ASMonaco_Basket|date=July 21, 2023|access-date=July 22, 2023|language=French}}</ref> On October 18, Walker made his debut for Monaco, scoring 2 points in ten minutes of play in a EuroLeague home win over [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-18 |title=Kemba Walker makes dull EuroLeague debut, but Monaco secures first win |url=https://basketnews.com/news-196067-kemba-walker-makes-dull-euroleague-debut-but-monaco-secures-first-win.html |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref> He only played in the EuroLeague during the season, averaging 4.4 points in 26 games.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Sam Perley |title=Kemba Walker Reaches Finality Of Playing Career, Finds Closure In Monaco |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/kemba-walker-reaches-finality-of-playing-career-finds-closure-in-monaco |access-date=28 November 2024 |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=15 November 2024}}</ref>

On July 2, 2024, Walker announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Kemba Walker Announces Retirement|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/kemba-walker-announces-retirement.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 2, 2024|access-date=July 2, 2024}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
===Charlotte Hornets (2024–present)===
On July 3, 2024, Walker was hired by the [[Charlotte Hornets]], joining Charles Lee's staff as a player enhancement coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Finalize 2024–25 Coaching Staff|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-finalize-2024-25-coaching-staff|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2024|access-date=July 3, 2024}}</ref> He later became an assistant coach for the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Inside Hornets' metamorphosis into the NBA's buzziest team|url=https://www.espn.ph/nba/story/_/id/48472147/nba-playoffs-2026-charlotte-hornets-kon-knueppel-lamelo-ball-play-miami-heat|website=espn.ph|date=April 14, 2026|access-date=April 15, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Kemba3-9592.jpg|thumb|right|Walker in a press conference at Middlesex Chamber of Commerce breakfast]]
Walker is the son of Paul and Andrea Walker.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/hschool/2007/06/19/2007-06-19_walk_this_way.html |title=Walk this way: Kemba can relax, now that he's settled on Connecticut |first=Ian |last=Begley |newspaper=[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]]|location=New York |date=June 19, 2007 }}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2011/03/11/2011-03-11_kemba_walker_and_dwight_hardy_both_make_bronx_proud_at_garden_but_walker_steals_.html |title=Kemba Walker and Dwight Hardy both make Bronx love at Garden, but Walker steals the spotlight |first=Mike |last=Lupica |author-link=Mike Lupica |newspaper=Daily News|location=New York |date=March 11, 2011 }}</ref> His parents met in his father's native [[Antigua]], while his mother is originally from [[St. Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands]] and was raised in the Bronx.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Robbins |first1=Lenn |title=Selfless star Walker is heart of Huskies |url=https://nypost.com/2011/03/31/selfless-star-walker-is-heart-of-huskies/ |access-date=March 5, 2019 |newspaper=New York Post |date=March 31, 2011}}</ref> He has two brothers, Akil and Keya, and two sisters named Sharifa and Kayla.<ref>{{cite web |title=KEMBA WALKER |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1857 |website=uconnhuskies.com |access-date=March 5, 2019}}
* {{cite web |last1=Armstrong |first1=Kevin |title=First NYC point guard to make NBA All-Star team since '03, Kemba Walker stays true to roots |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/first-time-all-star-kemba-walker-stays-true-nyc-roots-article-1.2964209 |website=Daily News|location=New York |access-date=March 5, 2019 |date=February 4, 2017}}</ref>

Walker grew up in the Sack-Wern Houses in [[Soundview, Bronx]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto1"/>

Walker is also a dancer. He performed three times at the [[Apollo Theater]] for the TV show ''[[Showtime at the Apollo]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=UConn's Kemba Walker retraces steps to Manhattan's Rice High School |newspaper=Daily News|location=New York |date=November 25, 2009 |first=Roger |last=Rubin |url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2009-11-25/sports/17938869_1_apollo-theater-big-dance-troupe|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110313105811/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2009-11-25/sports/17938869_1_apollo-theater-big-dance-troupe|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 13, 2011}}</ref>

On June 21, 2011, Walker released a mixtape in collaboration with [[DJ Skee]] and Skee Sports. The mixtape features songs inspired by and inspiring to Walker.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kemba Walker Drops The 'EZ Pass' Mixtape With DJ Skee |first=Aron |last=Phillips |newspaper=Dime Magazine |date=June 21, 2011 |url=http://dimemag.com/2011/06/kemba-walker-drops-the-ez-pass-mixtape-with-dj-skee/}}</ref>

In 2011, Walker signed a multi-year sponsorship deal with [[Under Armour]].<ref name="Under Armour"/> In 2015, Walker's contract with Under Armour expired. He subsequently signed with [[Jordan Brand]], a subsidiary of [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slamonline.com/kicks/kemba-walker-leaves-under-armour-for-jordan-brand/|title=Kemba Walker Leaves Under Armour for Jordan Brand|work=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]]|date=October 10, 2015|access-date=November 2, 2018}}</ref>

Walker made an appearance in the film [[Marty Supreme]] playing a member of the [[Harlem Globetrotters]] alongside fellow former NBA player [[Tracy McGrady]].<ref name="sports.espn.go.com">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/26/movies/marty-supreme-cameos.html |title=All the Cameos in 'Marty Supreme,' From Kevin O'Leary to Tyler, the Creator|publisher=[[The New York Times]] |date=December 26, 2025 |access-date=January 7, 2026}}</ref>
